quotes.text: The John Ackerman House West Side of River Road Teaneck, Bergen County, New Jersey Owner: Mr- Joseph KInzley, III Date of Erection: About 1800 Architect: Builder: John Ackerman Present Condition: Excellent, fully modernized Number of Stories: Two Materials of Construction: Foundation - sandstone Exterior walls - sandstone, gable siding Interior walls - plaster over wood lath Inside brick chimneys Roof - gambrel, wood shingles

note: Tranche 2, the Dutch trunk in America. Added by this pass as the node's PLAIN, SURVEYED, MEASURABLE case -- an ordinary Bergen sandstone gambrel with no fame attached to it, recorded on the same form and by the same district officer as the Steuben House, so the two can be read against each other without adjusting for the surveyor. Its materials line repeats the Steuben House's almost word for word (sandstone walls, gambrel roof, wood shingles) with one difference worth noticing: 'Inside brick chimneys' where the Steuben House has 'brick gables'. The inherited `chimney` slot forbids interior stacks flanking the ridge and makes gable-end stacks canonical; 'inside brick chimneys' is ambiguous between the two and is recorded rather than read either way.
